block.name: Burst Time Tagger CC
block.doc:
This block adds UHD-compatible time tags to a complex stream, generating one or more bursts inside a repeated pattern.
TIME MODEL:
- "Active period (s)" (period_s): duration of the region where bursts are allowed (e.g. a 5G-like frame of 10 ms).
- "Gap after period (s)" (gap_s): optional silent region after the active part, where no bursts are scheduled. This is useful when doing spectrum sensing between frames.
- Effective repetition period is: T_effective = period_s + gap_s
For each integer k = 0, 1, 2, ... (period index) and each offset o in "Offsets (s)", a burst is scheduled at:
t_burst = t0_usrp + k * T_effective + o
with "Burst length (samples)" samples.
For each burst: - "tx_time" and "tx_sob" are inserted at the first sample, - "tx_eob" is inserted at the last sample.
"Sample rate (Hz)" is used to convert sample indices into UHD time.
SPECIAL CASE: If "Offsets (s)" is an empty list, the block behaves as if it were [0.0] (one burst per active period, starting at the beginning).
TYPICAL USE CASES:
1) Simple periodic burst (no gap): period_s = 1e-3, gap_s = 0.0 offsets = [0.0] burst_len = number_of_samples_per_slot
2) 5G-like frame + silent sensing window: period_s = 10e-3 (10 ms of frame) gap_s = 5e-3 (5 ms silent gap) offsets = [0.0] (one burst per frame) burst_len = samples_in_10ms
In this case, the RF transmitter is active for 10 ms and then silent for 5 ms before the next burst.
PARAMETERS: - Sample rate (Hz): real USRP sampling rate. - Active period (s): length of the active region where bursts live. - Gap after period (s): silent time after the active region. - Burst length (samples): number of samples in each burst. - Initial USRP time (s): absolute UHD time of global sample index 0. - Offsets (s): Python list of offsets inside each active period, in seconds (e.g. [0.0, 0.001, 0.005]).
CALLBACKS: - set_samp_rate(samp_rate) - set_period(period_s) - set_gap(gap_s) - set_burst_len(burst_len) - set_t0_usrp(t0_usrp) - set_offsets(offsets_s)
